newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Investors more interested in Lithuania-Nomura.
newsitem.headline: Investors more interested in Lithuania-Nomura.

text.p: Foreign investors are becoming more interested in investing in Lithuania as the new right-wing government makes promises to privatise more companies in the Baltic state, Japanese investment house Nomura said on Monday.
Nomura was quoted as saying that foreign investors were interested in Lithuania by the government press office after Prime Minister Gediminaas Vagnorius met Nomura officials Friday.

"Nomura said that foreign investors are interested in the privatisation of big companies, especially in the telecommunications, energy and banking sectors and in Klaipeda sea port," the government said in a statement.

"The attention to positive reforms in Lithuania's economy is increasing and the number of foreign businessmen who would like to invest in Lithuanian companies being privatised is growing," the government quoted Hiromi Yamaji, the head of Nomura's investment banking department, as saying.

Vagnorius' right-wing Homeland Union government, which was swept to power last autumn, has committed itself to speeding up the privatisation process and attracting more foreign investment, an area where Lithuania is seen as a laggard.
On Friday, the government announced its intention to draw up a list of large companies in the energy, transport and telecommunications sectors to be sold over the next three years.
The government also said it would change legislation to allow "strategic" enterprises in these sectors to be privatised which the state is presently prohibited from selling.
